Q: How can I read/write from a flash memory connected through SPI on an embedded Linux system (ARM)? A:

Perhaps the device is locked by Das U-Boot, and ioctl UNLOCK is not implemented in your kernel's M25P80 driver.

I've seen that before. Refer to Erasing NOR flash memory: ioctl(MEMUNLOCK) return status.

Q: Setup environment using batch file for DotNet Framework Version Command line for easy way around A:

Got the working answer from one of the forums, for the complete solution to build with reference added.

We need to use /r option with compilation.

First add path using command below. Example:

C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v4.0.30319\csc.exe /t:exe /out:sample.exe sample.cs /r:ReferenceName.dll

After adding Path:

C:\test>csc /t:exe /out:sample.exe sample.cs /r:ReferenceName.dll

This solved my problem with reference.

Note: if reference is not in same directory as CS file it need to be added with its path.

Q: Erasing NOR flash memory: ioctl(MEMUNLOCK) return status A:

On newer Kernels (tested on 4.1.18) there is an device-tree option named "use-advanced-sector-protection;" When this is set, I was able to erase/write to protected flash-regions. It is also documented in the Kernel: Documentation/devicetree/bindings/mtd/mtd-physmap.txt
